headline: When to Call a General Contractor for Your Kitchen Countertop Replacement
articleBody:
Upgrading your countertops seems straightforward on the surface, but swapping out slabs can quickly involve base cabinet repairs, plumbing disconnections, and electrical updates. Knowing when a basic installer is enough versus when you need a licensed general contractor protects your home from hidden installation headaches.

Signs You Need a General Contractor
- Your existing base cabinets are unlevel or showing structural wear: Heavy stone surfaces require flat, reinforced bases. A general contractor inspects structural framing and levels cabinets before surfaces arrive.
- You are altering your sink, faucet, or cooktop locations: Moving plumbing pipes, gas supply valves, or dedicated 220V appliance circuits requires licensed trades and proper trade coordination.
- Your project involves removing or modifying perimeter walls: Creating extended breakfast bars or pass-through openings requires structural evaluation to ensure load paths remain safe.
- You want a coordinated tile or solid-slab backsplash: Integrating new countertop surfaces with electrical receptacle heights, under-cabinet lighting, and custom tile work goes beyond slab fabrication.
- You are pulling municipal permits for broader renovation work: If countertop replacement is part of an open-concept update, permit filings and inspections must be handled by a licensed professional.

What Can Change the Right Choice
If your project is a direct, same-footprint replacement on sturdy, modern cabinets with zero plumbing relocations, a specialty stone fabricator may handle the job. But if your project involves utility changes, structural reinforcements, or wall alterations, hiring a general contractor prevents costly mistakes and scheduling gaps between trades.
